questions.prompt: The Spaghetti-tree hoax aired on BBC's Panorama on April 1, 1957, and even advised viewers to place a sprig of spaghetti in a tin of tomato sauce and hope for the best if they wanted to grow their own. Who narrated this famous April Fools' Day broadcast?
questions.hint: It was not David Attenborough or Robin Day.
questions.explanation: The hoax was narrated by the respected broadcaster Richard Dimbleby, whose credibility helped convince many viewers that spaghetti really did grow on trees.

questions.prompt: In three dimensions, the limit is 12, so if you plan on kissing 13 people at once... sad. Which of the following is a real unusual Wikipedia article about this mathematical concept?
questions.hint: The real article is not about 'Touching coefficient' or 'Hugging ratio', those are made up terms with no mathematical basis.
questions.explanation: The kissing number is the maximum number of non-overlapping unit spheres that can simultaneously touch another unit sphere, which equals 12 in three-dimensional space.

questions.prompt: Sergeant Reckless was a horse that held an official rank in the US military, fought in the Korean War, and even participated in an amphibious landing. During the Battle of Outpost Vegas, how many solo trips did she make in a single day carrying ammunition to the front lines?
questions.explanation: During the Battle of Outpost Vegas in March 1953, Sergeant Reckless made 51 solo trips in a single day, hauling ammunition to the front lines and helping evacuate wounded soldiers on her return trips.

questions.prompt: The 65537-gon is a polygon with so many sides that it can be constructed with just a compass and straightedge, though it would look indistinguishable from a circle. According to the Wikipedia article, how many years did Johann Gustav Hermes spend working out the construction of this shape?
questions.explanation: Johann Gustav Hermes spent 10 years completing his construction of the regular 65537-gon, publishing his work in 1894; the manuscript is preserved in a large box at the University of Göttingen.

questions.prompt: What happens when noise music meets J-pop? The group Bis Kaidan formed from a collaboration between the idol group BiS and which noise music band?
questions.hint: The correct answer is not Merzbow or Incapacitants.
questions.explanation: Bis Kaidan was a collaborative project combining the Japanese idol group BiS with the legendary noise music band Hijokaidan, blending noise music with J-pop idol culture.

questions.prompt: This article explores the intersection of science and religion in a simple bacterium, focusing on a strain that evolved the ability to digest a synthetic material. What is the name of the enzyme these bacteria evolved to break down nylon byproducts?
questions.hint: 8 letters, starts with 'N'; named directly after the synthetic material it helps digest.
questions.explanation: The bacteria, a strain of Flavobacterium (later reclassified), evolved an enzyme called nylonase that allows them to break down and digest nylon manufacturing byproducts, a case often discussed in debates between evolutionary biologists and creationists.

questions.prompt: The Wikipedia article on Archaeoacoustics discusses the unusual idea that ancient pottery could act like a phonograph, accidentally recording ambient sounds such as voices while it was being shaped on a wheel. Which physicist proposed this intriguing theory in 1969?
questions.hint: 10 letters; his full name is Richard G. Woodbridge III, and he suggested spinning pottery could capture sound vibrations like grooves on a record.
questions.explanation: Richard G. Woodbridge III proposed in 1969 that the rotation of a potter's wheel might inadvertently etch sound vibrations, such as spoken words, into the clay in a manner similar to how a phonograph records sound, though this idea remains largely speculative and untested.

questions.prompt: Life lesson: if you see hunters chasing buffalo off a cliff, don't stand at the bottom. Which of the following is a real unusual historical site?
questions.hint: The real site is not named after antelope or cattle, since it was specifically used for hunting buffalo (bison).
questions.explanation: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Alberta, Canada, where Indigenous peoples once drove bison off a cliff to hunt them for thousands of years.

questions.prompt: In the 1970s, a group fought to end pay toilets across the U.S. and even published a newsletter called the Free Toilet Paper. Which of these is the real organization behind that campaign?
choices: Society for the Prevention of Coin-Operated Restrooms
National Alliance for Free Public Facilities
Committee to End Pay Toilets in America
questions.hint: The real group's name directly references 'Pay Toilets' and 'America,' unlike the vaguer or more generic-sounding names of the other choices.

article.title: Committee to End Pay Toilets in America

questions.explanation: The Committee to End Pay Toilets in America was a 1970s activist group that campaigned to abolish pay toilets in the United States, humorously naming its newsletter the Free Toilet Paper.

questions.prompt: Superhumps are periodic variations where a star thrusts in brightness during outbursts of SU UMa-type cataclysmic variable systems. By what percentage is the superhump period typically longer than the binary system's actual orbital period?
questions.hint: It's a small excess, just over 2 percent.
questions.explanation: The superhump period observed in SU UMa-type dwarf novae during superoutbursts is typically about 2% longer than the underlying orbital period of the binary star system, a discrepancy caused by the precession of an eccentric accretion disk.
